I don't really have an FLGS - the closest one is a 35 minute drive away and while their friendly enough, they don't host any events I'm terribly interested in and don't really give me any incentive to shop there. Still, if we're in the neighborhood we usually pop in and purchase something because we like to support our (semi) local businesses. That only happens once or twice a year though.

How many of us shop at our FLGS? Why shop their over say Amazon or Cool Stuff Inc?
How many of us have access to a Friendly Local Game Store (FLGS)? If you have one nearby, what keeps you coming back rather than buying online? Or do you mix and match when you purchase games?

The Raleigh area has quite a few, the one I frequent is The Gamers Armory in Cary. They give you a $10 credit on every $100 you spend, and their prices are not inflated. They don't have a HUGE selection, but they order games for you if its not in stock.

There a few things I think a FLGS has over an online source:

  • Immediate gratification - no waiting for shippment
  • Knowledgable staff with educated suggestions
  • Open gaming nights - A venue to play games with others, and experience new games you might not otherwise get to ever play
  • My store has a 50% off table for stuff that isn't selling well and they want to get rid of

The price you pay for these benefits is that your general game is more pricey than basically ANY online place.

For me personally, I have such a huge collection at this point that the only times I am looking to buy a game is if there's some sort of crazy deal on it, otherwise I generally can't justify the purchase. The staff at my local game store is pretty garbage, they (like most profitable game stores) have MTG as their primary source of business and you can really tell. I've never been able to mention a board game and have them know what I'm asking about, even if it's a really hyped game. The only time they've suggested anything for me, they just said "I don't know" to any follow up questions. Like, they knew to try to sell something, but weren't familiar with any of their product. In addition to this, the general sticker price hovers around 140-150% the amazon price. They are the only game in town, and have a good amount of turnout for their gaming nights, but I don't take advantage since I have multiple gaming groups already.

As a result, I occasionally like to check in at the FLGS, but 100% of the time I just sort of scan the place and go straight to the discount rack. 90% of the time the stuff on the rack is just barely under a CSI or amazon price, but occasionally you'll see a gem. Ultimately, I'd love to throw my money at a FLGS rather than the amazon mega-corp, but honestly, the big game store in my town cornered the market without being any good, and charges too much. If the prices were fairer, and the staff didn't flaunt how little they care about non-MTG customers, I'd be all about it.

I have Muse Comics & Games just 10 minutes from my house. I more or less grew up there with a bunch of my friends, going through phases of comics, Magic, D&D, Pathfinder, Warhammer 40k, much of which we still play today. I just love supporting a place that had that kind of impact on my life.

Other then SteamOS id say Ubuntu. Most games if they dont have a linux version can be run through wine, and you can run steam through wine to launch windows only games.

Edit: Arch Linux is a nice distro as well.
Does wine have a significant performance hit? I was thinking of dual booting windows just to get the best possible performance.

If your dual booting windows then you won't need wine to play games unless you REALLY wanna play them in linux. Wine has a very minimal performance requirement, and generally if a game works fine on windows it will run just fine on linux (performance wise) unless you have a memory leak.

I use debian and didn't have any trouble at all.

I was a steam for linux beta tester and didn't have much trouble either back then. Most people say that ubuntu is great for games and steam, but same goes for debian. And only ubuntu and debian are officially supported by steam, so I'd say those two are the best for gaming.

However, with a bit of tinkering and linux knowledge you can play in almost any distro.

Ubuntu, simply because most of the developers will be developing on it because it's what valve recommends. They recommend 12.04 but 15.04 works fine for everything for me.
